stance_summary: Verified: the Fed delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% after August CPI kept a tightening bias, SOFR printed 3.85 on 2026-09-17, and SR3 still prices 4.32 by Dec-2026 and 4.58 by Mar-2027. Canada’s overnight CORRA is 2.29 with only 2.58 priced by Dec-2026, CA 2Y is 3.27 versus US 2Y 4.76, and CA-US 2Y sits at -140bp. US labor/inflation gauges (75/72) dominate CA (38/55) while Canada core is near 2%. Inference: the clean USD expression is long USDCAD because the rate gap is already extreme in rates space while spot only reversed part of a still-negative 3m path. Unknown: CA official curve, CME futures positioning, NZ rates, and whether energy re-tightens CAD via the BoC pass-through channel.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Pay CORRA / receive SOFR or fade the already-extreme CA-US 2Y at -140bp (1y percentile 3.77, 5y 4.31). That rates gap is already at a multi-year cheap-Canada extreme, so more curve risk mainly duplicates a priced policy differential rather than capturing the still-incomplete FX adjustment.
expression_comparison.rationale: Dedicated USD-spot seat. The discrepancy is that USDCAD only partly reversed a still-negative 3m path after the Fed hike, while CA-US 2Y, SOFR-CORRA, and US-versus-CA labor/inflation already show a wide USD-policy advantage. A cross such as AUDCAD (1y/5y ~99.8th) adds unnecessary RBA/housing second-order risk when the weak CAD leg can be expressed directly against USD with carry support.

context_build.causal_mechanism: A delivered Fed hike plus a still-rising SOFR/SR3 path widens the USD funding and growth premium versus a BoC that remains 156bp cheaper overnight, with weak Canadian labor and contained core inflation limiting how fast CORRA can catch SR3. That policy-and-labor gap should keep USD bid versus CAD in spot.
context_build.path_to_current_price: ECB-cross USDCAD as of 2026-09-18 is 1.40105. The pair is still down 1.25% over 3m, then reversed +1.74% over 1m and +1.10% over 5d as August US CPI, >90% hike pricing into the Sep-16 FOMC, the 25bp hike, and the SOFR jump to 3.85 arrived. US 2Y rose 57bp over 1m and 9bp on 18-Sep to 4.76; CA 2Y fell 8bp on 17-Sep to 3.27, taking CA-US 2Y to -140bp. USDCAD therefore turned after a 3m CAD-firm stretch, but the 1y percentile is only 74.0 (5y 87.0), not a completed one-way squeeze.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before the cutoff: US inflation/labor heat, Canada 3% headline / ~2% core, BoC energy-pass-through minutes, and a large US-CA yield gap. Newly operative now: the hike was delivered (SOFR 3.62 on 16-Sep to 3.85 on 17-Sep), SR3 still prices additional tightening (Dec 4.32, Mar 4.58, 12m 4.755), and the 5d CA-US 2Y move of -15bp (z -2.17) arrived alongside only a 1.10% USDCAD rise. The Saudi Oman STS workaround also modestly reduced the extreme oil-supply tail that had been a CAD support.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: Current pricing assumes the Fed hike is largely a USD event already absorbed in G10 (EURUSD -1.89% 1m, GBPUSD -2.07% 1m) and that CAD can remain relatively firm because BoC minutes keep an energy-inflation option open and CORRA is allowed to grind toward 2.58 by Dec and ~3.65 by 2028 without a USD/CAD catch-up.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The assumption that USDCAD has already done enough of the Fed-versus-BoC work. Rates have priced a near-extreme Canada cheapness; spot has not finished the 3m reversal, and Canada’s labor gauge (38) versus US labor (75) does not support CAD holding a high real-rate/commodity premium against a still-hiking Fed.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: USDCAD 1.40105 on 2026-09-18 (packet mid; not a broker quote). Change: +0.11% 1d, +1.10% 5d (z 1.61), +1.74% 1m (z 1.23), -1.25% 3m. Volatility: 20d RV 5.17%, 60d 4.31%. Marginal driver of the latest 5d rise is the Fed-delivery/SOFR jump and the 5d CA-US 2Y widening, not a WTI residual (USDCAD~WTI r^2 0.017, stale) or a tight rates beta (USDCAD~CA-US_2Y r^2 0.022, weak). Carry screen: US versus CA 2Y differential 140bp over 4.37 vol.

historical_reference.distribution: USDCAD 1y percentile 74.0 / 5y 87.0 with a still-negative 3m return. US 2Y is 4.76 at 99.8th 1y / 88.0th 5y after a +57bp 1m rise. CA 2Y is 3.27 at 97.8th 1y but only 58.5th 5y. CA-US 2Y is -140bp at 3.8th 1y / 4.3rd 5y. Those are discovery ranks, not the thesis.
analogs: US 2Y +57bp 1m analog 2022-03-23 (level 2.13): forward +59bp 1m / +88bp 3m as the first hiking cycle extended.
US 2Y +56bp 1m analog 2023-02-16 (level 4.62): forward -70bp 1m / -50bp 3m, a failed-extension episode at a similar yield level.
CA-US 2Y 1m analog 2025-01-30 at a similar -145bp level after a -17bp 1m widening: forward -5bp 1m / +25bp 3m, i.e. the spread often stops widening once this cheap.
CA-US 2Y analog 2024-12-18 (level -130bp): forward -3bp 1m / -20bp 3m, a continued-widening case.
historical_reference.regime_differences: 2022 hiking-cycle analogs started from much lower US 2Y levels; today’s 4.76 2Y and a just-delivered 25bp hike are closer to the mixed 2023 episodes. The Jan-2025 CA-US analog shows the rate spread may already be extreme enough to stop widening, which is why the residual is in spot, not in buying more Canada cheapness on the curve. Energy is also two-sided now (Saudi STS workaround versus weaker shock absorbers), unlike a clean 2022 oil-shock CAD bid. Packet FX is a 2026-09-18 ECB cross, two days before cutoff.

independent_checks: Policy-path check: SOFR 3.85 versus CORRA 2.29; SR3Z6 4.32 and SR3H7 4.58 versus CRAZ26 2.58 and CRAH27 3.13. The overnight gap is 156bp and the Dec gap is still ~174bp.

Temperature gauges: US labor 75 / inflation 72 / activity 69 / consumer 74 versus CA labor 38 / inflation 55 / activity 66 / consumer 45, plus Canada August CPI 3% with core near 2% versus August US CPI that kept a Fed tightening bias.

Positioning/carry: CFTC TFF CAD leveraged funds remain net short CAD (-39,022; -10.9% of OI) even after +16,426 covering in the week to 2026-09-15; USDCAD carry screen 140bp 2Y differential / 4.37 60d vol supports long USD versus CAD. AUDCAD at ~99.8th percentile confirms CAD, not AUD, is the weak commodity-dollar leg.
context_build.flow_and_positioning_check: CFTC TFF as of 2026-09-15: CAD OI 358,186 (1y 81.7th). Leveraged funds are still net short CAD but covering; asset managers also covered (net -9,386 after +20,622). Dealers cut a long CAD book (-33,493). Ownership can explain some of the 5d USDCAD squeeze via short-covering, but the residual short is not a one-sided crowded long-USD extreme. CME daily FX positioning is unavailable. Broad USD index is stale (as_of 2026-09-11). Flow is a contributor, not a substitute for the policy/labor gap.

policy_path_check.pricing_summary: US: SOFR 3.85 on 2026-09-17 after the 25bp hike; SR3 prices 4.32 by Dec-2026, 4.58 by Mar-2027, 4.755 by Sep-2027; packet US terminal context 4.6025 by 2028-08. CA: CORRA 2.29; 1m CORRA Dec-2026 2.58 (+29bp); 3m CORRA Mar-2027 3.13 and mid-2028 ~3.65. NZ policy path is unavailable. AU is not required for this pair: AONIA 4.35 with 4.86 priced by Mar-2027.
policy_path_check.rationale: The live US and CA overnight-linked paths are in the packet and show the Fed still priced for more tightening while BoC is priced only for a shallow grind that does not close the 156-174bp near-term gap. That is the policy content that USDCAD has only partly translated after a still-negative 3m spot path.

trade.thesis: FACT: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; SOFR 3.85; US 2Y 4.76; SR3 still prices 4.32/4.58 at 3m/6m. FACT: CORRA 2.29; CA 2Y 3.27; CA-US 2Y -140bp; Canada labor gauge 38 versus US 75; Canada core near 2%. FACT: USDCAD 1.40105 is +1.74% 1m but still -1.25% 3m. INFERENCE: the USD-versus-CAD policy and labor gap is cleaner in spot than in rates because the sovereign/OIS differential is already extreme, while EURUSD/GBPUSD have already sold 1.9-2.1% 1m and AUDUSD still has AONIA/AU 2Y carry against a short. UNKNOWN: whether energy pass-through forces a faster BoC catch-up, and whether CAD short-covering completes without further USD upside.
trade.mispricing: Rates have already marked Canada unusually cheap versus the US (CA-US 2Y 3.8th 1y percentile). USDCAD has not finished translating that into spot: 3m still negative, 1y only 74th percentile, and the 5d rates move (CA-US 2Y z -2.17) exceeded the still-moderate 1.10% FX move. That is a path discrepancy, not a claim that a regression residual is fair value (USDCAD~CA-US_2Y r^2 is 0.022).
why_now: The Sep-16 hike is now in the SOFR print and in SR3, so the USD overnight benchmark has jumped while CORRA has not.
The 5d CA-US 2Y widening is the largest short-horizon rates impulse in the packet and arrived with USDCAD still below a completed 3m recovery.
Saudi STS workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail that had been a CAD offset, while BoC minutes still treat energy as a risk rather than a delivered tightening cycle.
Sidecar is flat; funding vig on the full $100m at 3.85% SOFR makes a defined USD-spot book preferable to staying idle.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:Canada August inflation holds at 3%, core stays near 2%
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
trade.invalidation: Thesis is invalid if the US path is fully recast as one-and-done while CORRA/CA 2Y reprice toward SR3/US 2Y enough to close the policy gap, or if Canada labor/core reheat and restore a CAD-tightening bid, or if a renewed energy shock reasserts CAD via the BoC pass-through channel. No invented numeric stop.
catalysts: Next US inflation/labor prints that keep the SR3 hike path intact after the delivered 25bp.
BoC communication or Canadian labor/CPI that fails to close the 156bp overnight gap.
Oil remaining contained after the Saudi Oman workaround, limiting CAD’s energy offset.
Continued CAD leveraged-fund residual shorts after incomplete covering.
principal_risks: Energy shock re-widens CAD via BoC pass-through even if US policy stays hawkish.
US 2Y analog risk: the 2023-02-16 episode reversed a similar-sized 1m yield rise.
CAD short-covering already started; a squeeze can fade USDCAD without changing the rates gap.
Packet FX is two days old; CA official curve and CME positioning are missing.
A cross-led AUDCAD unwind could move CAD without a clean USD impulse.

remit: express macro views through USD spot whenever a defensible USD pair exists

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Delivered Fed hike plus a still-steeper SOFR/SR3 path versus a cheap, labor-soft BoC leaves USD under-expressed in USDCAD after only a partial 3m reversal.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: US data that keep SR3 hiking while Canada labor/core keep CORRA from closing the 156-174bp gap.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: Fed path recast as one-and-done and/or BoC/energy re-tightens CAD enough to close the policy gap.

paper_actions.rationale: Empty sidecar. Deploy $55m of the $100m gross cap in the single cleanest USD spot: long USDCAD. Size is below cap to leave room if energy/CAD covering volatility rises, but large enough versus 3.85% SOFR vig if spot continues the incomplete 3m reversal. Trusted code must transact at the packet mid; no authored mark.
paper_actions.thesis: USD policy/labor premium versus a cheap BoC is already extreme in CA-US 2Y and SOFR-CORRA; express it in USDCAD spot, not a cross and not more curve.
